summary: Hashing turns 'is X in this collection?' from O(N) into O(1) average. Three patterns cover ~90% of interview hashing problems: (1) frequency counting with HashMap<value, count>; (2) seen-before set for first-repeat / pair-sum-target / contains-duplicate; (3) prefix-sum map for 'subarray with sum K' style — store prefix sums in a map, look for (currentSum − target). Master long keys when sums can overflow int.

thoughtProcess.title: 1. HashMap vs HashSet vs int[] frequency.
thoughtProcess.body: If values are bounded (≤ 10^5 or so), an int[] is faster and avoids autoboxing. If values can be 10^9 or negative, use HashMap<Integer, Integer>. If you only need membership, HashSet is enough.

thoughtProcess.title: 2. Pair-with-target = complement search.
thoughtProcess.body: Walk the array once. For each x, check if map contains (target − x). If yes, you've found a pair. Otherwise put x in the map. Beats O(N²) brute.

thoughtProcess.title: 3. Subarray sum = prefix sum + map of seen sums.
thoughtProcess.body: currentSum after i is S[i]. A subarray (l, r] has sum S[r] − S[l]. So 'exists subarray with sum K' becomes 'exists earlier prefix S[l] = S[r] − K' — a single map lookup.

thoughtProcess.title: 4. Subarray sum = 0 special case.
thoughtProcess.body: Look for repeated prefix sums (S[l] == S[r]) OR a prefix sum that equals 0 (subarray from index 0). Use long for the running sum if values can swing wide.

thoughtProcess.title: 5. Count distinct in sliding window.
thoughtProcess.body: Slide a window of size B over the array. Maintain HashMap<value, count>. On window slide: increment new, decrement old; remove key when count hits 0. Distinct count = map.size().

thoughtProcess.title: 6. First repeating / unique — single pass with map.
thoughtProcess.body: For first repeating: build freq map (full pass), then walk array left-to-right returning the first element with freq > 1. For 'count of elements with freq == 1' (unique count): two-pass or freq map + size filter.

thoughtProcess.title: 7. Pair-count problems with duplicates need care.
thoughtProcess.body: Counting pairs (i,j) i<j with A[i]+A[j]=B: walk once, for each x add freq[B-x] to ans BEFORE putting x in map (this enforces i<j and handles duplicates: e.g. [2,2] with B=4 contributes 1 not 4).

thoughtProcess.title: 8. Encode a pair/coordinate into one long key.
thoughtProcess.body: When you need a HashMap/HashSet keyed by a 2-tuple (i,j) with bounded ranges, avoid a wrapper object or nested map. Pack both ints into one long: key = ((long) a << 32) | (b & 0xFFFFFFFFL). The mask on b is essential — without '& 0xFFFFFFFFL' a negative b sign-extends and corrupts the high 32 bits. Faster and lower-garbage than nested maps, with a single O(1) lookup.

thoughtProcess.title: 9. Reach for the right container by the question, not habit.
thoughtProcess.body: HashSet = pure membership/distinct (no counts). HashMap = you need an associated value (count, index, sum). LinkedHashMap = deterministic insertion-order iteration. TreeMap = sorted keys / floor / ceiling. Plain HashMap gives NO order guarantee and the order can change between JVM versions, so never rely on its iteration order for the answer.

commonMistakes.title: Forgetting that HashMap.get returns null for missing key
commonMistakes.wrong: int c = freq.get(x);  // NullPointerException when x not present
commonMistakes.why: HashMap returns null, autounboxing to int crashes. Use getOrDefault.

commonMistakes.title: Double-counting pairs in 'sum equals B'
commonMistakes.why: If you pre-build freq then iterate, you count each pair twice (once from each end). Single-pass with complement-before-put gives i<j cleanly.

commonMistakes.title: Prefix sum subarray=0 missing the 'sum already 0' case
commonMistakes.wrong: for i in 0..N-1: sum += A[i]; if seen.contains(sum): return true; seen.add(sum);
commonMistakes.why: Without the sentinel, you miss subarrays that start at index 0. Insert 0 first.

commonMistakes.title: Int overflow in prefix sum
commonMistakes.wrong: int sum = 0; for (int x : A) sum += x;   // overflows when N=1e5 and |A[i]|=1e9
commonMistakes.right: long sum = 0; for (int x : A) sum += x;
commonMistakes.why: 1e5 × 1e9 = 1e14 — far beyond int range. Always use long for prefix sums when |A[i]| can be large.

commonMistakes.title: Distinct-in-window: forgetting to remove keys with count 0
commonMistakes.wrong: freq[A[l]]--;  // when count becomes 0 the key still occupies a slot — map.size() over-reports distinct
commonMistakes.why: map.size() counts keys, not non-zero values. Drop the key when count hits 0 so size reflects true distinct count.

commonMistakes.title: First repeating: returning by position in map iteration
commonMistakes.wrong: for entry in freq.entrySet(): if entry.getValue() > 1: return entry.getKey();   // HashMap has no order!
commonMistakes.right:
// Build freq with full first pass, THEN walk the array in order:
for (int x : A) if (freq.get(x) > 1) return x;
commonMistakes.why: HashMap iteration order is undefined. To find the FIRST repeating, walk the original array.

commonMistakes.title: Longest-zero-subarray storing latest index instead of earliest
commonMistakes.wrong: map.put(prefixSum, i);  // always overwrites → only most-recent index kept
commonMistakes.right: if (!map.containsKey(prefixSum)) map.put(prefixSum, i);  // keep earliest only
commonMistakes.why: For longest zero-sum subarray you want the EARLIEST occurrence of each prefix sum so that (currentIndex − earliestIndex) is maximised.

commonMistakes.title: Comparing boxed Integer keys/values with == instead of .equals
commonMistakes.wrong:
Integer a = map.get(x), b = map.get(y);
if (a == b) { ... }   // '==' compares references; true only by luck for -128..127
commonMistakes.right:
if (a != null && a.equals(b)) { ... }
// or unbox: if (a != null && b != null && a.intValue() == b.intValue())
commonMistakes.why: Autoboxing caches Integer objects for -128..127, so == accidentally works for small values and silently breaks for values > 127. Use .equals (or compare primitive int) for Integer objects.

commonMistakes.title: Using contains(x) on a Map when you meant containsKey(x)
commonMistakes.why: Set.contains checks membership; Map exposes containsKey (keys) and containsValue (values, O(N)). Confusing them checks the wrong side or fails to compile.

commonMistakes.title: Relying on HashMap iteration order for the answer
commonMistakes.wrong:
Map<Integer,Integer> m = new HashMap<>();
... for (var e : m.entrySet()) out.add(e.getKey());  // order undefined
commonMistakes.right:
Map<Integer,Integer> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();  // preserve insertion order
// or re-scan the ORIGINAL array to impose the needed order
commonMistakes.why: HashMap makes no ordering promise; its layout depends on hashes/capacity and can change between JVM versions. If the expected output order is 'first appearance' or 'sorted', use LinkedHashMap/TreeMap or re-scan the source.

keyPatterns.name: Frequency Map (count occurrences / queries)
keyPatterns.when: How many times does each value appear? Answer membership / count queries.

keyPatterns.name: HashSet for distinct / duplicate / first-repeat
keyPatterns.when: 'Are there duplicates?' or 'first element to repeat as I scan left-to-right'.

keyPatterns.name: Complement Pair Search (sum == B)
keyPatterns.when: 'Does some pair sum to B?' or 'count pairs with sum B'.

keyPatterns.name: Complement Pair Search (difference == B)
keyPatterns.when: 'Count pairs (i,j) with |A[i] − A[j]| = B' (or signed diff).

keyPatterns.name: Prefix Sum + Map (subarray sum = K)
keyPatterns.when: Continuous subarray with given sum (positive, negative, zero).

keyPatterns.name: Common-Elements with Multiplicity
keyPatterns.when: Intersection respecting duplicates (min(countA, countB) per value).

keyPatterns.name: Sliding Window with HashMap (distinct in window)
keyPatterns.when: Maintain stats over a moving window of fixed or variable size.

keyPatterns.name: Pair/coordinate key via long packing
keyPatterns.when: You need a set or map keyed by two bounded ints (grid cell, edge, composite pair) and want to avoid object keys or nested maps.

keyPatterns.name: First-seen-order output with LinkedHashMap/LinkedHashSet
keyPatterns.when: You must dedupe or count but emit results in the order elements first appeared.

edgeCases: Empty array → frequency map empty, set empty; first-repeat returns -1.
All elements same → first repeat is A[1]; distinct = 1; count unique = (N == 1 ? 1 : 0).
Subarray zero-sum with single zero in the array → return true; the prefix-sum map should include the sentinel 0 first.
Prefix sum overflow → use long; relevant when N=1e5 and |A[i]| can reach 1e9.
Pair sum count when B − x == x → don't add x with itself; the complement-then-put ordering already prevents this if duplicates exist.
Pair difference with B == 0 → counts (x, x) pairs; result = Σ C(freq[x], 2).
Distinct-in-window when window size B > N → output one entry: distinct of entire array.
Longest zero-sum subarray with sum reaching 0 at index i → length i+1, requires the (0, -1) sentinel in the index map.
Subarray with given sum (positive ints only) — sliding window (two pointers) is simpler and O(N), no map needed.
Common elements with multiplicity — order should be insertion order of B (or A, problem-specific); confirm expected order.
Long-key packing with negative low half: forgetting '& 0xFFFFFFFFL' on b lets a negative b sign-extend and clobber a's bits — two different pairs then collide.
Integer autobox cache boundary: two Integer keys equal to 200 satisfy .equals but fail ==, while two equal to 100 pass == by accident — test with values > 127.
Adversarial hash collisions degrade HashMap ops to O(N); Java 8+ treeifies large buckets to O(log N), but encode/randomize keys if collisions are a concern.
Order-sensitive grader: an unordered HashSet/HashMap answer may fail even when the multiset is correct — switch to LinkedHashMap or sort before comparing.
containsValue in a hot loop is O(N) per call, turning an O(N) algorithm into O(N^2); precompute or invert the map instead.
